newsitem.title: LATVIA: PAREKS SAYS WILL KEEP LEAD IN 1997 - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: PAREKS SAYS WILL KEEP LEAD IN 1997 - REPORT.

text.p: Pareks Bank believes its profit in 1997 will beat that of rival Unibanka and is working on Russian investment projects and bond issues, Pareks deputy president Viktor Krasovitsky was quoted on Tuesday as saying.

"Unibanka's costs incurred by the vast network of branches will not allow it to show profit figures that compete with the figures of Pareks," Krasovitsky told Dienas Bizness newspaper in an interview.
Pareks' investments this year are focussed on attracting investment to a number of Russia's regions.
"There are no big projects in Latvia for the time being and at the same time attracting investment to Russia's regions is much simpler," Krasovitsky told the newspaper.
"The funds of both Western investors and the bank are being placed in Russia's economy," Krasovitsky added.
Talks on issuing and distributing municipal bonds have taken place with Leningrad region, Chelyabinsk and other municipal governments, Krasovitsky said.
An agreement has been reached in principle about attracting investment worth $150 million to the development of the Leningrad region infrustructure.
